articles.summary: Promoted Málaga slump to 4-0 defeat at the Bernabéu. Suzuki scores hat-trick in Freiburg’s win against Werder. Real Madrid maintained their perfect start to the season in La Liga with a comfortable 4-0 home ⁠win over promoted Málaga on Sunday, scoring three times inside 30 minutes before adding a…
body: Jude Bellingham’s brilliant solo opener, an own ⁠goal by the Málaga goalkeeper ⁠Alfonso Herrero and ​a sharp Kylian Mbappé volley effectively settled the contest before half-time, with substitute Arda Guler wrapping up the victory in added time at ⁠the Bernabéu.
The win lifted Madrid to nine points from three matches, two clear of Atlético Madrid and Alavés. Barcelona, fourth on six points with a ⁠game in hand, host Rayo Vallecano on Monday.

Bellingham opened the scoring in the 19th minute ‌with a superb burst through the middle, collecting a loose ball near the edge of the area, gliding past three defenders and firing low beneath Herrero. They ​doubled their lead seven minutes later after Herrero could only palm out Mbappé’s effort. Bellingham headed the rebound back towards goal and, as Herrero and a teammate collided while trying to clear, the ball ended up in the net.

articles.title: Fernandes fires hat-trick as Manchester United fight back to thrash Ipswich
articles.summary: To follow the claiming of both major footballer of the year awards by scoring a hat-trick in Manchester United’s first home game was some Bruno Fernandes act, and points to an intent to continue his stellar form of last season.
body: Ipswich Town came to scythe Michael Carrick’s side via the pace of Julio Enciso, Issa Diop and Daizen Maeda, and when Leif Davis gave them a 29th-minute lead victory was on.
However, the contest turned with Marcelino Núñez’s slip as the break neared. Suddenly Fernandes was rifling in a left-foot bullet and from this juncture United cuffed Gary O’Neil’s team aside.

In 12 second-half minutes (56-68), United scored three times – the first, a Jacob Hargreaves own goal, the next two, Fernandes’s strikes that made his three for the day, Bryan Mbeumo completing the rout.

Carrick was emphatic that the pathetic 2-0 downing by Hull was “just one game” and he was proved correct – certainly going forward. Davis’s opener was derived from holes being punched in the rearguard, and Chuka Akpom’s added-time consolation came from sloppy defending from Lisandro Martínez that allowed Ensico to set up the replacement.

articles.title: Why Man Utd goal was allowed to stand - despite Maguire 'handball'
articles.summary: The handball law often serves to confuse supporters - and it reared its head again as Harry Maguire celebrated putting Manchester United in front against Ipswich Town.
body: The ball came off the United defender's arm, before he then moved a few yards forward into the box and his shot found its way into the back of the net.
Surely the goal would be ruled out. After all, any handball by the scorer means the goal must be disallowed.
Apart from one very important point - Maguire did not actually score the goal.
Maguire's effort was going well wide, and deflected into the back of the net off Jacob Greaves. It was officially an own goal.

articles.summary: Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal says his wife made him take his espresso machine from Tigers' clubhouse to Los Angeles
articles.summary: It's confirmed. A beloved espresso machine that used to reside in the Detroit Tigers' clubhouse is gone. It now sits in Tarik Skubal's kitchen in Los Angeles. Skubal confirmed the news to reporters during his return to Detroit for this weekend's series between his current Dodgers and his former…
body: "I'll wear it," Skubal said Saturday of taking the machine, per the Detroit Free Press. "I did buy it, but I guess I'll wear it."

Per the Free Press, Skubal said that that machine is now in his house in Los Angeles. It's not clear what kind of machine it is. But this is certainly not a one-button budget plastic model that you might find in your office break room.

The machine had become a fixture in the Detroit clubhouse. And espresso had become a ritual for the Tigers, so much it that MLB.com published an article on the team’s coffee habit in February during spring training.

Per that story, an espresso setup at the team’s Lakeland, Florida clubhouse even had a name: Casey's Cafe. Skubal and then Tigers pitcher Casey Mize went in together to buy the machine. Like Skubal, Mize was also traded at the August MLB trade deadline, about 120 miles south of Skubal to the San Diego Padres.

articles.title: Tech trouble leaves Chelsea game ref without comms
articles.summary: When referee Michael Oliver emerged for the second half at Stamford Bridge on Sunday something important was missing - his communications pack.
body: For 45 minutes as Chelsea beat Brighton 4-3, a set of Premier League officials had to work without radio sets for what may have been the first time in 20 years.
The referee, his assistants, the fourth official and the video assistant referee (VAR) team at Stockley Park could not talk to each other.

Referees were first fitted with a microphone and an earpiece at the start of the 1999-2000 season, and while this did not become permanent initially, an upgrade allowed for more sophisticated radio technology to be introduced from the 2006-07 campaign.

There have been problems with the battery packs or the communication link in the past. We have seen games held up while a technician fiddles with the device strapped to the arm of the referee or his assistant.

Despite taking an early second half lead thanks to the in-form Carrick Njinko, Leeds United Under-21s fell to a narrow Premier League 2 defeat on the road to Liverpool Under-21s.

Scott Gardner’s side started well in Merseyside with a first notable chance coming after nine minutes. Callum Mills, Njinko and Freddie Lane combined to force Liverpool’s goalkeeper, Bailey Hall, into action.

articles.title: Man Utd 5-2 Ipswich: What O'Neil said
articles.summary: Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil speaking to Sky Sports: "Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.
body: "To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn't. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.
"It is a complicated rule - handball if it's the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.
"But no problem. I'm not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

"We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don't want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand."

articles.title: Fernandes hat-trick helps Man Utd come from behind to beat Ipswich
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as Manchester United came from behind to beat Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win of the season.
body: It looked like being a difficult afternoon for Michael Carrick's team early on. Julio Enciso and Daizen Maeda both forced smart stops from Senne Lammens before Abdul Fatawu skinned Luke Shaw and fed Leif Davis to side-foot the opener high into the United net.

Old Trafford was edgy at that point, with United having lost to Hull on the opening weekend. But the game turned when Marcelino Nunez slipped over. Matheus Cunha robbed the Chilean midfielder and found Fernandes, who slammed the ball home with his left foot.

Bryan Mbeumo should have completed the turnaround early in the second half only to strike the bar from close range, but United did not have to wait long. Their second was not without controversy, however, as Harry Maguire escaped punishment for a handball.

Had his shot gone straight into the net then it would have been disallowed but because the attempt was diverted in by Jacob Greaves, it was allowed to stand. Moments later, United took the game away from Ipswich as Greaves' unfortunate afternoon continued.

articles.title: Moses Itauma’s next move is now fascinating – here are his options
articles.summary: Comment: The 21-year-old, arguably the most-hyped boxer in the world, suffered his first loss as the towel came in after he punched himself out
body: The more fights you watch, the fewer surprises you see. That’s not to say there aren’t still upsets; they just don’t seem as seismic. The clues are there all along, it just depends how much attention you pay to them.

To be clear, this is not a claim that The Independent predicted that Filip Hrgovic would beat Moses Itauma on Saturday. The idea that Itauma would break down the Croatian, stop him late, and fulfil his world-title prophecy seemed sensible.
Still, two indisputable factors surrounding their clash – for the vacant IBF heavyweight belt – were discussed throughout fight week, just never with enough emphasis.

Those factors were Hrgovic’s durability, and Itauma’s inexperience down the stretch. And with these in mind, it suddenly doesn’t seem so shocking that Itauma punched himself out to the point that he had nothing left by the ninth round.

articles.title: England seal series victory against Pakistan as Robinson shines
articles.summary: Joe Root’s second stint as England captain is off to a flying start as his side cruised to a comfortable 194-run win over Pakistan at Lord’s to seal the series, going 2-0 up with a game to go.
body: On a pitch that was heavily weighted towards the bowlers, England advanced their lead by 32 runs on day four to set Pakistan a huge total of 389 to win.
Mohammad Abbas tore through England's tail order on Sunday, taking a haul of five wickets, as the hosts were bowled out for 208 runs.

Pakistan were unable to surpass the hosts' lead, with a ruthless Ollie Robinson, back at his happy hunting ground at Lord's, taking four wickets on Sunday to bring up a match haul of eight as the hosts rattled their way through the visitors' batting line-up.
"I think the guys have shown great adaptability," Root said. "We've overcome some difficult situations when we were at 80-4 to get the total that we did.
